terms.grammar: indeclinable noun and adverb; as a noun with a genitive
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: the opposite of satis and nimium; it has no comparative of its own (minus, minimē). With a genitive, too little of: frondis parum; with an adjective or a verb, “not … enough”: parum cautī, not careful enough.

evidence: Mart. 14.220.1: nōn satis est ars sōla cocō
terms.comment: Plainly “not enough”, without the reproach of parum (see enough).

phrases.latin: nam quod salūtī satis est, dēlectātiōnī parum est
phrases.english: for what is enough for health is too little for pleasure

phrases.latin: hoc lautum est parum; illud rēctē: iterum sīc mementō
phrases.english: this one hasn’t been rinsed enough; that one’s right: remember to do it that way again

phrases.latin: cūr frondis parum est, strāmenta dēsunt?
phrases.english: why is there too little fodder, and no straw?

phrases.latin: nōn quī parum habet, sed quī plūs cupit, pauper est
phrases.english: the poor man is not the one who has too little, but the one who wants more

phrases.latin: mātūtīna parum cautōs jam frīgora mordent
phrases.english: the morning cold is already biting those who are not careful enough

phrases.latin: nōn satis est ars sōla cocō
phrases.english: skill alone is not enough for a cook

sources: Lewis & Short: parum · Lewis & Short: satis
